intelligence_report.executive_summary: Fifteen months into the five-year plan, the board faces a strategic decision point. Digital operational delivery exceeds targets: mobile transactions run at 2.4× baseline, uptime holds at 99.6%, and cost-to-serve on retail customers has fallen 18%. The capital position remains comfortable at 16.4% CET1, 240 basis points above the internal floor. Two concentrations require board attention: real estate exposure has drifted to 31.2% against a 25% internal guideline, and digital lending NPLs have reached 9% against an original 6-7% assumption. The CEO recommends pivoting the digital lending product mix toward secured SME credit and lowering the FY28 digital revenue target from 18% to 16%. The board must decide whether to approve the strategic refresh, maintain the original path, or adopt a more conservative posture.
intelligence_report.framing: Board Chair and Chief Executive Officer · 25 June 2025

recommendations.text: Board — approve the strategic refresh with Option 3 (16% digital revenue target, pivot to secured SME digital lending) or select an alternative path
CEO — present a detailed execution plan for the secured SME digital lending pivot, including underwriting competence assessment, customer relationship strategy, and revenue yield assumptions
CRO — propose a transition plan for the existing unsecured digital book that quantifies potential near-term loss crystallisation and capital impact
CFO — provide ROE trajectory data for Q3 2025 and assess whether current performance tracks to the FY26 sustained 18% ROE target
CEO — explain what specific aspects of cohort dynamics were insufficiently understood at strategy approval and what analytic process will prevent similar misses in the secured SME pivot
CRO — present a credible plan to bring real estate concentration back within the 25% guideline, including timeline, business line impact, and governance controls
Board Risk Committee — assess whether the two concentration breaches warrant external review of risk management and capital allocation frameworks before approving the strategic refresh
